## WF5 - the owner's weekly report

Runs Monday morning and writes `reports/weekly-YYYY-MM-DD.md`.

**The report is the numbers. The narrative is a courtesy.**

Every figure is computed by the review service from SQL, using the same definitions the
Metrics page and `query.mjs` use, windowed to one calendar week. There is no week-scoped
copy of any metric - E8-S1 asserts each appears exactly once, and a second implementation of
a definition is what that story exists to prevent.

The model writes one paragraph and **never a figure**. That is enforced by code in
`review-ui/weekly.mjs`, not by asking nicely: a commentary carrying a number is dropped whole
and the report says "Narrative unavailable this week". A prohibition holds about two runs in
three; code settles it (CLAUDE.md).

The caveats are computed from state. While `baseline_status = 'none'` the report carries the
illustrative line, and **that line removes itself** when the row changes, with nobody editing
prose.

### Why this one call is allowed to fail quietly

Every OTHER model call in this system stops its run when it fails - BUG-028 was caused by
leniency turning an outage into a logged `success`.

This call is the declared exception, and `check-failure-routing.mjs` names it as one with
this reason: **the narrative is not the product.** The report is the figures, and they were
already computed before this node ran. A failure here must produce a report that says
"Narrative unavailable this week" - not no report.

The next node is what makes that true: it reads the commentary if there is one and passes
nothing if there is not. It never invents a paragraph.
